previous_description: A database index for query optimization. Paradigm-neutral: covers B-tree and hash indexes (relational), compound and multikey indexes (document stores), vector approximate nearest neighbor indexes (HNSW, IVF), inverted indexes (search engines), geospatial indexes, and secondary indexes (wide-column stores).
definition: A lookup structure the data store engine maintains alongside a collection's or view's records, keyed on one or more of its fields with a declared access method (B-tree, hash, inverted, ANN, geospatial and similar). Queries use it to locate matching entries without scanning the whole collection.

distinguish_from.when: the declaration is a PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE or FOREIGN KEY constraint whose purpose is rejecting invalid data, even if the engine backs it with an implicit index; model a separate Index only when the index is declared explicitly.

the thing called an 'index' is itself the container of documents or vectors, such as an Elasticsearch/OpenSearch index (collectionType SEARCH_INDEX) or a Pinecone index, rather than an auxiliary structure over another container's fields.
the code or documentation describes the shape of a read or write (key condition, filter, frequency) rather than a structure declared to the engine.
the structure holds derived rows that are queried directly, such as a materialized view or continuous aggregate, rather than pointers back to the source records.

standard_reference: None in ISO/IEC 9075: indexes are implementation-defined; the de facto reference is the vendor CREATE INDEX statement (e.g. PostgreSQL CREATE INDEX).
code_evidence: A CREATE INDEX / CREATE UNIQUE INDEX statement (optionally with USING gin|hnsw|ivfflat or a WHERE predicate) in a migration script, or a migration-tool call such as op.create_index, add_index, or knex table.index().
An ORM or schema declaration of an index: Prisma @@index, Django Meta.indexes, SQLAlchemy Index(...) in __table_args__, JPA @Table(indexes=@Index(...)), or a Mongoose schema.index({...}) call.

Engine-specific index provisioning: a MongoDB createIndex({...}, {partialFilterExpression, sparse}) call, DynamoDB GlobalSecondaryIndexes/LocalSecondaryIndexes in CloudFormation or Terraform, or a Cassandra CREATE CUSTOM INDEX / SAI statement.

attribute_descriptions.name: unique
attribute_descriptions.description: Boolean that is true when the index rejects duplicate key values across indexed entries (CREATE UNIQUE INDEX, MongoDB {unique: true}); set it only when the index declaration itself enforces uniqueness, and otherwise leave it false or unset.

notes: The method enum mixes access methods with key shapes: COMPOUND/MULTIKEY are orthogonal to BTREE. The fields attribute is a plain string, with no per-field sort direction or opclass. The Elasticsearch 'index' is claimed by both the collection and namespace definitions. Unique indexes overlap with ValidationRule UNIQUE. AccessPattern→Index has redundant aggregates and uses relationships.
